title: Make engram source fast on Windows: skip the 5-second git submodule script when the index has no gitlinks and merge repeated rev-parse calls
outcome: Make engram source fast on Windows: skip the 5-second git submodule script when the index has no gitlinks and merge repeated rev-parse calls
acceptance: Per-step timings of `engram source --root <Engram main checkout> --json` on Central are recorded on this item before and after the change, with the same machine and repository state

When the index contains no gitlink (mode 160000), source observation does not run `git submodule status --recursive`; when gitlinks exist, submodule detection and the child filter, line-ending and dirt guards behave exactly as before, proven by tests with and without a submodule

Repeated Git queries in one observation are merged where Git can answer them in one invocation (for example rev-parse --show-toplevel, --absolute-git-dir and the HEAD and tree reads), without weakening the start and end equality checks that detect HEAD or worktree movement during the read
source_id output is byte-identical before and after for the same repository state; the 10-second warning and the 60-second minimum timeout are unchanged
On Central the observation of the Engram main checkout completes under the 10-second warning threshold, with the measured number recorded
